evidence: Tables from McSnow reference columns on the capped lunar build, by the flake law over their superparticles; the closure they define followed McSnow within its bands on nine of the eleven resolved box runs of the fifth test and overstated the loss in 0.1 mm/h snow from -15 C (1.48, 1.65 in e-foldings). No lunar observation; the cap stands in for a breakup law.
reading_rule: Below a cloud base h1 (m above the freezing level), dF/dz = s k [(F/F(h1))/(F^(z)/F^(h1))]^-q F going down, s the subsaturation over ice. Each family matches its references by ln F(h1) against their fluxes at h1 (linear between neighbours, held at the ends) and averages ln k, q and ln F^ with those weights; F^ is the least-squares line of a reference flux on height through its layers from 0 up to the one holding h1 + 500 m. A snow top H between the families' tops interpolates the two at the same height with weight (H - top_S)/(top_D - top_S) on D, each by depth below its own top; H at or below top_S takes S, and at or above top_D takes D, by depth below H, held at the deepest layer. Heights in a family are its references' own: z_ref = z + top_f - H for the single-family cases. k is per metre at unit subsaturation.
assumptions: k and q carry the thermodynamics of the 301 K design ladder at each height; a column warmer or colder than the ladder takes them as they are.
A snow top above 32.56 km takes family D by depth below the top, held at the deepest layer, where the capped flakes have gathered under the cap; no run tested such a top.
In 0.1 mm/h snow from -15 C, where nearly all the snow sublimates, the closure overstates the loss by about five points of the flux at the cloud base: the stated limit of its adoption.

sensitivity_10cm.note: The 10 cm references in place of their 14 cm twins; the others unchanged.
